title: ForkMesh code roadmap · Jul 18–Aug 1, 2026
body:
Complete two-week, code-only delivery plan covering every technical item in the supplied roadmap. All implementation runs in parallel AI-assisted lanes from July 18 through July 29; July 30 through August 1 is reserved for integration, regression repair, and the final release gate.

## Parallel implementation lanes

- Native planning, tests, specifications, and release: #433, #434, #443, #474
- Git, protected writes, dependencies, large objects, and merge: #435, #436, #437, #454, #455, #467, #468, #469
- Discovery, availability, receipts, and preservation proof: #438, #439, #465, #466
- Browser contribution, identity, collaboration, social, and review: #440, #446, #447, #459, #460, #463
- Private data, scanning, and operator policy: #448, #449, #450, #451
- Migration, low-bandwidth and nearby sync, routes, bundles, and releases: #441, #445, #452, #453, #461, #472
- Headless execution, events, packaging, and independent deployment: #442, #456, #457, #464, #470, #471, #473
- Core independence and product quality: #444, #458, #462

## Complete 30-topic coverage

1. Clear capability statement and quick start: #444 generates it from passing code probes.
2. Public discovery and search: #438 covers search, activity, rankings, verified maintainers, and clone actions.
3. Standard Git compatibility: #435 owns the executable matrix; #441, #455, and #467 close bundle, dependency, and large-object rows.
4. Authenticated push and protected refs: #436, #437, #454, and #469 cover credentials, signer policy, approvals, checks, and atomic merges.
5. Hosted-system bridges and migration: #445 provides the provider-neutral adapter; #464 and #471 carry events and checks.
6. No-install contribution: #446 covers browser signing, generic sessions, offline queueing, and node handoff.
7. Human-readable sync status: #439 and #465 show repository and per-object evidence, quorum, pin, and verification state.
8. Conflict-safe collaboration: #440 defines deterministic convergent folds for every collaboration object family.
9. Recoverable scoped identity: #447 covers passkeys, hardware authenticators, rotation, social recovery, organizations, delegation, proofs, and trust scopes.
10. Private repository confidentiality: #448 encrypts all private storage; #449 handles revocation, rekey, and recovery.
11. Node-local abuse controls: #450 implements seeding, rate, block, community-list, report, quarantine, and local-removal policy.
12. Secret and malware hygiene: #451 uses one scanner across hooks, publication, and mirror intake.
13. Low-bandwidth, unreliable, and offline operation: #441, #452, and #472 cover bundles, selective resumable sync, local discovery, and nearby links.
14. Multiple network routes: #453 covers direct, proxy, overlay, and LAN-only configuration, health, and leak prevention.
15. Workflow and deployment integration: #454, #464, #470, and #471 cover gates, outbound delivery, isolated runners, signed checks, streams, and deployment consumers.
16. Package dependency use: #455 covers stock dependency clients, immutable locks, provenance, and verified fallback.
17. Desktop, command-line, headless, service, image, cluster, small-device, and appliance operation: existing clients plus #442, #456, and #473.
18. Transparent service boundaries and failure independence: #457 publishes the manifest and proves independent bootstrap and default-service loss.
19. Core workflow independence: #458 removes optional account extensions from required repository paths and schemas.
20. Fast repository preservation onboarding: #445 imports complete context; #439, #461, and #466 produce the resilience result.
21. Portable discovery signals: #459 covers social, mirror, production-use, and security-review assertions.
22. Familiar terminology: #460 standardizes every user-facing interface while retaining compatibility aliases.
23. Complete review workflow: #454, #463, #468, and #469 cover conversations, suggestions, ownership, patchsets, stacks, comparisons, queue, strategies, conflicts, and client parity.
24. Availability proof dashboard: #439, #465, and #466 cover clone challenges, quorum, diversity, routes, ref and artifact coverage, offline state, and risk codes.
25. Releases and artifacts: #461 covers signed releases, binaries, checksums, software bills of materials, provenance, documentation, package references, and verified downloads.
26. Complete self-hosting: #442, #456, #457, #470, and #473 cover every service role, runner, package, backup, restore, health, and metrics.
27. Protocol specifications and compatibility: #474 publishes schemas, interfaces, vectors, threat model, and reference verifier; #443 gates them.
28. Product quality: #462 enforces interaction, local-first performance, search, graph, visual, and accessibility budgets.
29. Honest capability comparison: #435 and #444 provide code-backed matrices and a deployment chooser without external-product themes.
30. Priority order and completion: milestone deadlines, contract freeze July 22, feature freeze July 29, and #443 complete the whole set by August 1.

## Delivery rules

- Dates and dependency text drive execution; numeric priority keeps a stable triage order with #443 reserved as the final closure blocker.
- July 18–22: freeze shared contracts and land foundations.
- July 23–25: complete daily Git workflows and integrate parallel feature surfaces.
- July 26–29: finish secure collaboration, open operations, packaging, and cross-component wiring.
- July 30–August 1: accept no new feature scope; fix regressions and pass #443 twice from clean checkouts.
- Non-code positioning and business copy are excluded; every technical consequence in the supplied roadmap is linked above.

Done means all 42 linked issues meet their automated acceptance criteria, all generated artifacts are current, and the signed release gate passes for one commit by August 1, 2026.

events.body:
Two-week code-only delivery plan for native planning, Git compatibility and protected writes, deterministic collaboration, repository discovery and availability, offline transfer, and operator readiness.

## Parallel workstreams

- Planning and CI: #433 + #434 → #443
- Git workflow: #435 → #436 + #437 → #441 → #443
- Discovery and status: #438 + #439 → #443
- Collaboration and operations: #440 + #442 → #443

## Delivery rules

- July 18–24: land foundations and daily-workflow surfaces.
- July 25–29: complete resilience and operator work in parallel.
- July 30–August 1: freeze feature scope; integrate, fix regressions, and pass #443.
- Market positioning, funding, and speculative features are out of scope.

Done means every linked issue meets its automated acceptance criteria and the integrated release gate passes by August 1, 2026.
